findings.source_passage: you could almost see that thought turn in him as he turned, and pace in him as he paced; so completely possessing him, indeed, that it all but seemed the inward mould of every outer movement.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 3, description of Ahab's obsessive pacing before mustering crew
findings.why_it_matters: This passage is interpretively important — it establishes the physical-metaphysical fusion of Ahab's thought and movement before the chapter's central confrontation, and its imagery of thought as 'inward mould' is critically noted.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence about thought turning in him as he turned; it is brief and carries essential character-establishing weight for this scene.

findings.source_passage: If money's to be the measurer, man, and the accountants have computed their great counting-house the globe, by girdling it with guineas, one to every three parts of an inch
findings.source_locator: Ahab's reply to Starbuck's 'Nantucket market' speech
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical elaboration ('accountants have computed their great counting-house the globe, by girdling it with guineas') is Ahab's characteristic mad-logic voice; the draft reduces it to 'If money's to be the measurer, man, then let me tell thee,' losing the signature grandiosity.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full accounting-house-of-the-globe clause; it is a brief but distinctively voiced passage that contextualizes the chest-smiting gesture that follows.

findings.source_passage: Stubb cautiously whispered to Flask, that Ahab must have summoned them there for the purpose of witnessing a pedestrian feat.
findings.source_locator: paragraph describing assembly before Ahab's first question
findings.why_it_matters: This comic aside is a signature Stubb moment that establishes the crew's baffled normalcy before Ahab's revelation — a tonal and character beat the critical tradition notes as part of Melville's dramaturgy.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert one sentence capturing Stubb's whispered conjecture about a 'pedestrian feat' before Ahab's vehement pause and first question.

findings.source_passage: Starbuck paled, and turned, and shivered.
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, after the goblets are quaffed
findings.why_it_matters: A small but iconic three-beat sentence marking Starbuck's horror at the completed oath; its absence slightly flattens the closing tableau.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the three-word cadence 'Starbuck paled, and turned, and shivered' after the hiss of the quaffed spirits.

findings.source_passage: Attend now, my braves. I have mustered ye all round this capstan … O men, you will yet see that—Ha! boy, come back? bad pennies come not sooner.
findings.source_locator: Ahab's speech at the capstan before the lance-crossing ceremony
findings.why_it_matters: This speech contains Ahab's invocation of 'fisherman fathers' and his interrupted vision ('you will yet see that—'), a narratologically significant fragment; its absence removes texture from the ritual.
findings.suggested_fix: Include at least the 'noble custom of my fisherman fathers' clause and the interrupted exclamation as interpretive atmosphere for the drinking ceremony.

summary: The draft preserves all high-priority signatures — the pasteboard masks speech verbatim, the doubloon nailing, Ahab's confession about Moby Dick, the oath, and the framing prose — but omits several medium-weight voice passages (the thought-turning description, the full globe-girdling clause, Stubb's pedestrian-feat aside) that collectively thin the chapter's rhetorical richness without rising to regeneration threshold.
